source: (By the Mainmast; Starbuck leaning against it.)

My soul is more than matched; she’s overmanned; and by a madman! Insufferable sting, that sanity should ground arms on such a field! But he drilled deep down, and blasted all my reason out of me! I think I see his impious end; but feel that I must help him to it. Will I, nill I, the ineffable thing has tied me to him; tows me with a cable I have no knife to cut. Horrible old man! Who’s over him, he cries;—aye, he would be a democrat to all above; look, how he lords it over all below! Oh! I plainly see my miserable office,—to obey, rebelling; and worse yet, to hate with touch of pity! For in his eyes I read some lurid woe would shrivel me up, had I it. Yet is there hope. Time and tide flow wide. The hated whale has the round watery world to swim in, as the small gold-fish has its glassy globe. His heaven-insulting purpose, God may wedge aside. I would up heart, were it not like lead. But my whole clock’s run down; my heart the all-controlling weight, I have no key to lift again.
[A burst of revelry from the forecastle.]

Oh, God! to sail with such a heathen crew that have small touch of human mothers in them! Whelped somewhere by the sharkish sea. The white whale is their demigorgon. Hark! the infernal orgies! that revelry is forward! mark the unfaltering silence aft! Methinks it pictures life. Foremost through the sparkling sea shoots on the gay, embattled, bantering bow, but only to drag dark Ahab after it, where he broods within his sternward cabin, builded over the dead water of the wake, and further on, hunted by its wolfish gurglings. The long howl thrills me through! Peace! ye revellers, and set the watch! Oh, life! ’tis in an hour like this, with soul beat down and held to knowledge,—as wild, untutored things are forced to feed—Oh, life! ’tis now that I do feel the latent horror in thee! but ’tis not me! that horror’s out of me! and with the soft feeling of the human in me, yet will I try to fight ye, ye grim, phantom futures! Stand by me, hold me, bind me, O ye blessed influences!

modern_en.title: Chapter 38 — Dusk
paragraphs: By the mainmast. Starbuck leaning against it.

My soul is more than matched — she's overpowered, and by a madman! What an unbearable sting, that sanity should lay down its arms on such a battlefield! But he drilled deep down and blasted all my reason out of me! I think I see his impious end, but I feel that I must help him reach it. Whether I will or not, the unspeakable thing has tied me to him, towing me with a cable I have no knife to cut. Horrible old man! "Who's above me?" he cries — yes, he would be a democrat to all above, but look how he lords it over all below! Oh! I can plainly see my miserable duty: to obey while rebelling, and worse still, to hate with a touch of pity! For in his eyes I read some terrible grief that would shrivel me up if I had it. Yet there is still hope. Time and tide flow wide. The hated whale has the whole round watery world to swim in, as a small goldfish has its glass globe. His heaven-insulting purpose — God may push it aside. I would take heart, if my heart were not like lead. But my whole clock has run down. My heart is the weight that controls everything, and I have no key to wind it again.
(A burst of revelry from the forecastle.)

Oh, God! To sail with such a heathen crew that have so little touch of human mothers in them! Whelped somewhere by the sharkish sea. The white whale is their demigorgon. Listen! Those infernal orgies! That revelry is forward. Notice the unbroken silence aft! It seems to me a picture of life. Out in front, through the sparkling sea, shoots the gay, embattled, bantering bow — but only to drag dark Ahab after it, where he broods inside his cabin at the stern, built over the dead water of the wake, and further on, hunted by its wolfish gurglings. The long howl thrills me through! Quiet, you revelers, and set the watch! Oh, life! It is in an hour like this, with the soul beaten down and held to knowledge — as wild, untamed creatures are forced to feed — oh, life! It is now that I feel the hidden horror in you! But it is not me! That horror is outside of me! And with the soft human feeling still in me, I will try to fight you, grim phantom futures! Stand by me, hold me, bind me, O you blessed influences!

modern_da.title: Kapitel 38 — Tusmørke
paragraphs: Ved stormasten. Starbuck læner sig op ad den.

Min sjæl er mere end overmandet — hun er overvældet, og af en vanvittig! Hvilket uudholdeligt stik, at fornuften skal lægge våbnene på sådan en slagmark! Men han borede dybt ned og sprængte al min fornuft ud af mig! Jeg tror, jeg kan se hans ugudelige ende, men jeg føler, at jeg må hjælpe ham frem til den. Hvad jeg så vil eller ej, har det usigelige bundet mig til ham og slæber mig med et tov, jeg ingen kniv har til at skære over. Forfærdelige gamle mand! »Hvem er over mig?« råber han — ja, han ville være demokrat over for alle ovenover, men se, hvordan han spiller herre over alle nedenunder! Åh! Jeg kan tydeligt se min elendige pligt: at adlyde, mens jeg gør oprør, og, endnu værre, at hade med et strejf af medlidenhed! For i hans øjne læser jeg en eller anden frygtelig sorg, som ville skrumpe mig sammen, hvis jeg havde den. Og dog er der stadig håb. Tid og tidevand flyder vidt. Den forhadte hval har hele den runde, våde verden at svømme rundt i, som en lille guldfisk har sin glaskugle. Hans himmelfornærmende hensigt — Gud kan skubbe den til side. Jeg ville tage mod til mig, hvis mit hjerte ikke var som bly. Men hele mit ur er løbet ned. Mit hjerte er den vægt, der styrer alting, og jeg har ingen nøgle til at trække det op igen.

Åh, Gud! At sejle med sådan et hedensk mandskab, som har så lidt af menneskemødre i sig! Hvalpet et sted af det hajagtige hav. Den hvide hval er deres demigorgon. Hør! De helvedes orgier! Den gammen er forude. Læg mærke til den ubrudte tavshed agter! Det forekommer mig et billede af livet. Foran skyder gennem det funklende hav den glade, krigeriske, drillende bov — men kun for at slæbe mørke Ahab efter sig, hvor han grubler inde i sin kahyt i agterenden, bygget over kølvandets døde vand og længere hen, forfulgt af dets ulvagtige klukken. Det lange hyl gennemrusker mig! Vær stille, I festende, og sæt vagten! Åh, liv! Det er i en time som denne, med sjælen slået ned og holdt fast til viden — som vilde, utæmmede væsener tvinges til at æde — åh, liv! Det er nu, jeg føler den skjulte rædsel i dig! Men det er ikke mig! Den rædsel er uden for mig! Og med den bløde menneskelige følelse stadig i mig vil jeg prøve at kæmpe mod dig, dystre fantomfremtider! Stå ved min side, hold mig, bind mig, O I velsignede påvirkninger!
